info.name: LocalLearn — ASUS APIs (from Mac)
info.description:
APIs the Mac (dev client) calls on the ASUS (server) for the LocalLearn track.

Two services run on the ASUS:
- **Ollama**  → embeddings + generation  (port 11434)
- **Qdrant**  → vector DB               (port 6333, REST)

## Setup
The collection variables default to the ASUS LAN IP (192.168.1.19). If your ASUS IP changes, edit the `asus_ip` variable once (Collection → Variables) and every request follows.

To hit services locally *on the ASUS itself* instead, set `asus_ip` = `localhost`.

Models and collection name mirror the Day 2–4 scripts:
- `embed_model` = nomic-embed-text (768-D)
- `gen_model`   = llama3.1:8b
- `collection`  = day4_beacon_docs

## Suggested run order (Qdrant)
Health → Create collection → Upsert points → Query points → Count → Delete.
Upsert/Query bodies use a tiny 4-D dummy vector so you can exercise the API by hand without generating a real 768-D embedding first. For a real end-to-end test, grab an embedding from **Ollama → Generate embedding**, then paste it into the upsert/query body (and set the collection's vector size to 768).

item.name: Ollama (:11434)
item.description: Local LLM server. Used by day2/day3/day4 scripts for embeddings (`/api/embeddings`) and grounded generation (`/api/chat`).

request.description: Bare GET on the root returns 'Ollama is running'. Fastest smoke test that the ASUS service is reachable from the Mac.
Lists locally-pulled models on the ASUS. Confirm nomic-embed-text and llama3.1:8b are present here before running the scripts.
Details for one model: parameters, template, context length, quantization.
Download a model onto the ASUS. Run once to provision nomic-embed-text / llama3.1:8b. stream=false waits for completion and returns a single final status.
THE Day 2–4 embed call. One string → one 768-D vector under `embedding`. Copy that array into the Qdrant upsert/query bodies for a real end-to-end test.
The Day 4 generation call. Grounded RAG prompt with numbered context. stream=false returns the full answer under `message.content`. temperature 0 keeps reruns comparable.
Simpler prompt→completion endpoint (no chat roles). Handy for quick model sanity checks.

item.name: Qdrant (:6333)
item.description:
Vector DB REST API. The qdrant-client calls in day3/day4 map 1:1 to these HTTP endpoints.

Note: the sample upsert/query bodies use a 4-D dummy vector so you can drive the API by hand. For a REAL test, use a 768-D embedding from Ollama and set the collection's vector size to 768.

request.description: Readiness probe. 200 = Qdrant container is up and serving. Fastest reachability check from the Mac.
What `client.get_collections()` calls under the hood — used by the scripts' connect() as a real round-trip health check.
PUT /collections/{name}. size=4 matches the dummy vectors below; for real nomic-embed-text data set size=768. Distance Cosine = the Day 2/3 metric.
Status, vector config, and point count for one collection. 404 here is how `collection_exists` decides existence.
PUT /collections/{name}/points. wait=true blocks until the write is applied (what the scripts use). Replace vectors with real 768-D embeddings for an actual test.

POST /collections/{name}/points/query — the Day 3/4 retrieval call. `query` is the query embedding; returns top-k nearest points with score + payload. Use a real 768-D query vector from Ollama for meaningful results.
How many points are stored. Quick check that an ingest actually landed (Day 5 debugging: 'did anything get stored at all?').
Page through stored points without a vector query. Inspect what payloads actually got indexed — the 'is it retrieval or storage?' debugging seam.
DELETE /collections/{name}. The scripts drop + recreate each run so re-ingests are clean.
